title: Routing policy matrix: dedicated-first routing + hosted fallback and model-variant safeguards
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Implement a deterministic routing policy that prefers customer-dedicated GPU capacity but safely falls back to hosted endpoints or smaller model variants when capacity/region constraints are hit. This ticket scopes the policy matrix, enforcement guards (cost/latency caps, data-residency blocking), telemetry, and a canary rollout plan.
background: Customers with Dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput and strict isolation. However, during unexpected saturation or regional outages, we need transparent and controllable fallback behavior. Current behavior is ad-hoc: requests either queue, fail, or route to hosted with little observability. We need a policy layer that encodes business priorities (customer tier, region restrictions, SLA) and programmatic safeguards to avoid cost/regression blasts.
goals: Define a deterministic policy precedence order: region affinity -> dedicated pool availability -> tier-based throttling -> hosted fallback -> model-variant fallback
Add server-side safeguards: per-tenant cost cap, max hosted tokens per minute when falling back, and latency SLO gating to prevent slow-hosted routing
Expose controls in Console: toggle hosted-fallback, preferred fallback model variants, and per-customer budget caps
Provide full telemetry and audit logs for routing decisions for investigations and billing reconciliation
Ship a canary rollout with simulation on real traffic history before global enablement
non_goals: Full rewrite of autoscaler policies (this will be coordinated but lives in a separate ticket)
Persisted customer-configured routing policies in this iteration (we will support a limited knob set first)
Changing model catalog/quantization tooling (we will reference existing variants only)
acceptance_criteria: Routing engine implements precedence order and returns decision metadata on each request (route_target, reason_code)
Fallback to hosted is governed by per-customer token rate and cost caps; exceeded caps produce deterministic errors and audit entries
Model-variant fallback chooses a pre-approved compatible variant (same architecture, compatible tokenizer) and annotates response with variant_id
Console exposes a per-customer hosted-fallback toggle and a dropdown to select allowed variant families
End-to-end tests covering: dedicated route success, capacity-saturation -> hosted fallback, hosted-rate-limit enforcement, region-blocking + error path
Canary run (5% traffic for one week) with dashboards: routing distribution, latency P50/P95/P99, cost delta vs baseline, and audited routing events
Runbooks for incidents where hosted fallback is disabled and dedicated pools are full
decisions: Prefer dedicated pools within the request region unless a hard data-residency block exists
Hosted fallback will be limited by a per-customer hosted_token_rate cap configurable in Console (default 1000 tokens/min)
Model-variant fallback only allowed to variants in an approved compatibility list; automatic quality regression prevention via lightweight prompt-evals
Routing decision will be emitted as structured headers and stored in audit-events for billing reconciliation
tradeoffs: Strict dedicated-first routing preserves isolation but increases request failures under saturation; hosted fallback reduces failures but risks cost spikes and degraded quality
Enforcing conservative hosted caps avoids cost surprises but makes fallback ineffective for bursty workloads unless autoscaler or pre-warm is used
Choosing a small set of approved model variants reduces regression risk but limits fallback effectiveness for specialized tasks
